div.head: Iudex 11
div.ab: Sepe etiam praui iudices iudicium peruertunt uel respectant et non finiunt causam, donec uultus eorum impleatur; et quando indicant, non opera, sed munera considerant.

Oft eac ða ðwyran deman for heora gitsungae þone dom geuferiað oððe hyne awendað ⁊ ne geendiað ná þa spæce, ær heora seod bið afylled; ⁊ þan þonne hy demað, ne sceawiað hy ná þa spæce, ac þa medsceatas.

Often also, through greed, wicked judges defer or pervert cases, and don’t complete [them] before their purses are filled; and then they make determinations, not considering the cases, but [considering] the bribes.

Ferner schieben die verderbten Richter wegen ihrer Habgier oft den Urtheilsspruch auf oder verdrehen ihn und bringen nimmer die Klagesache zu Ende, bevor ihr Geldbeutel gefüllt wird; und dann, wenn sie Urtheil sprechen, ziehen sie nie die Klagesache, sondern die Lohngelder in Betracht.

Further, corrupt judges, because of their greed, often postpone or pervert the judgment and never bring the suit to an end before their purse is filled; and then, when they give judgment, they consider not the suit but the bribes.
div.note: Isidore, Sent. III 52.11. The Quadripartitus's ‘uultus’ (face) reflects a confusion of OE ‘seod’ (purse) with ‘seo’ (pupil) or ‘gesihð’ (sight), Liebermann suggests.
